messages:
erin: proposing a small RFC follow-up — microbatch-aware soft-pin + reclamation window for small allocations (embeddings/kv chunks). we keep seeing jitter when tiny batches thrash the offload path :thinking:

nate: interesting. you mean tag allocations with current microbatch id and avoid evicting them for X ms?

erin: yeah. idea is: on alloc, attach `microbatch_id` and `soft_pin_until = now + window_ms` if batch size < threshold. eviction skips soft-pinned pages unless memory pressure > hard_threshold. reduces re-populate churn.

vikram: would help real-time tails. curious about memory overhead — small batches are common for async single-user requests though. what window_ms are you thinking?

erin: starting point 50-200ms. heuristic: window_ms ~ avg microbatch latency * 1.5. default 100ms. config knobs per-tenant.

jen: how does this interact with prefix/KV cache? those are also hot but longer lived. we should make the soft-pin tier lower priority than explicit cache pins.

erin: agreed. priority order: explicit cache_pin > recent_inflight_soft_pin > normal resident. eviction must still be able to preempt soft-pin under severe pressure.

alloc-bot: [telemetry] soft_pin events: count=4321 window_ms=100 avg_retained_bytes=1.2MB pressure_evictions=12

sophie: two other things: 1) tag should be cheap (one extra 8-byte header) and stored in page metadata, 2) we need a fast scan-free admission test for evictor to ignore soft-pins cheaply. maybe a bitmap per-allocator generation?

nate: bitmap + per-tenant resident estimate sounds good. evictor can check tenant_resident + expected_reclaimable and fast-path skip if reclaimable < shortfall. avoids per-page reads.

jen: edge case: a microbatch that spans multiple requests (retries) — microbatch_id should be ephemeral and tie to in-flight token. need GC of tags after window too.

erin: yep. GC: soft_pin_until timestamp lives in metadata; background sweeper clears stale tags. also expose metric `soft_pin_fallthroughs` when evictor had to preempt despite pin.
